details: CONFIRMED by the live probes. agent_rows() calls worktree_of(_first_cwd(path)) only; the brief asked "mapped by brief or worktree".
Because relay's own rules tell agents to use git -C from the primary checkout, the cwd rule misses most build, fix and check agents,
so agent minutes, build minutes and the fixed cycle are all undercounted, and the median is taken over a biased sample of 8.
rules/queue.md now tells the front to "Use that number for --time": a wrong number is now presented as measured, worse than a guess
labelled as one. HIGH: the change's own promise (pass case 1, actuals per change) fails on ordinary use.
evidence: estimate for a new item: 17m (... of 8 changes)
outside-worktree types: runner 30, worker 26, fixer 24, checker 20, critic 11, scout 10, thinker 8
failing_case: Live data, 28 Oct: in ~/.claude/projects/-Users-amidman-relay, 130 of 284 subagent transcripts have first cwd /Users/amidman/relay
(26 of them delegate:worker, 24 fixer, 20 checker), because briefs say "git -C and absolute paths; never cd into it".
Closed item taken by wt/drop-plugins: its worker transcript names .worktrees/drop-plugins in the prompt but cwd is /Users/amidman/relay,
so `relay queue estimate` leaves the item out. Of 105 closed items with taken_by, 8 are measured; those show e.g.
"150 est 1 agents (0 build) 149 wall checks-keep-two-finding-lists..." and 0 build for 6 of 8.
Printed estimate: 17m, against 26-53 agent minutes measured for the cycle on 24 Oct. The brief's pass case
"within 1.5x for at least 9 of 12 changes of the 24 Oct sample" is not met (builder's Gap line says so).
Should: an agent whose prompt/brief names `.worktrees/<name>` (or the brief file of the change) is counted to that change even when
its cwd is the primary checkout, and the 24 Oct sample reaches 9 of 12 within 1.5x.
fix_hint: In agent_rows, when the first cwd names no worktree, take the worktree from the first user message (the brief's `Worktree:` line or
the first `.worktrees/<name>` path in it); test with a fixture transcript of that shape; then measure the 24 Oct sample and record it.
pass_cases: 1. Transcript with first cwd /r and first user message "Worktree: /r/.worktrees/c1 ... " of type delegate:worker, 7 min -> one AgentRow("c1", "delegate:worker", 420).
2. Transcript with cwd /r/.worktrees/c1 (today's case) -> still AgentRow("c1", ...).
3. Transcript with cwd /r and no worktree or brief named -> no row.
4. Transcript naming two worktrees (a train brief naming riders) -> counted once, to the worktree it works in (the first `Worktree:` line), not to every name.

5. On the 24 Oct sample of 12 changes, estimate() of the other changes is within 1.5x of measured agent minutes for >= 9 of 12 (a recorded measurement in the item or a test over a fixture of their numbers).
reason: Cases 1-4 met (tests/test_queue_estimate.py:107,110,113,127 pass). Pass case 5 (24 Oct sample, 9 of 12 within 1.5x) was not measured by the fixer and has no test or recorded measurement; live output shows est 40-50 against 135-266 agent minutes for several items.
findings.summary: agents are tied to a change only by their first cwd, so the ones run from the primary checkout (git -C) are lost: 97 of 105 closed items get no actual and the estimate rests on 8 partial changes
